newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's April open unemployment rises to 4.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's April open unemployment rises to 4.3 pct.

text.p: Mexico's open, or base, unemployment rate rose to 4.3 percent during April compared to 4.2 percent in March, the National Statistics Institute said on Tuesday.
INEGI said in a statement the jobless rate compared to 6.2 percent unemployment during April of last year.
It said that the metropolitan areas that showed the greatest declines were Monclova, Durango, Iraputo, Tampico, Saltillo, Queretaro, Toluca and Tlaxcala.

INEGI said that without the seasonal factors, the open unemployment rate in April would have been 4.12 percent, or almost one percent lower than in the previous month, showing tha the unemployment rate is trending downwards.
"The seaonally adjusted data shows that the number for April, 1997 is the lowest in the last 28 months," it said.
INEGI defines open unemployment as members of the workforce older than 12 who have searched for work but have not worked more than one hour a week during a month.

The Rate of General Pressure, which measures those in work looking for a new job as well as open unemployment, was 8.0 percent during April compared to 9.6 percent in the same period a year earlier. The Rate of Partial Joblessness and Unemployment, which
includes open unemployment and those who have worked less than 35 hours a week due to market conditions, fell to 6.1 percent during April versus 7.7 percent in April last year.
The Alternative Open Unemployment Rate, which includes open unemployment as well as those who have given up looking for work, was 5.2 percent in April compared to 7.0 percent in April last year.
